headline: Notes and screenshots on phases and gates

changes.title: Numbers, yes/no, dates, choices and links
changes.now: A run detail can be a number, yes/no, date, choice or link (context: rows:number, due:date), and a step can ask for a number, yes/no or date as evidence. Each gets the right box and is checked as it's typed. Text from a plan or a parent run converts only when that's certain; anything else waits for a person, and nothing that uses it goes ahead. A checklist without typed values works as before.
changes.before: Every run detail and evidence value was text.
changes.where: The start form, the run's Details, evidence boxes and the step-type editor

changes.title: Contract 2 reads Flightdeck 2.0 runs and versions
changes.now: flightdeck run, runs and process with --contract 2 read 2.0 versions and runs, with each value's kind, its stored text, a typed value and any conversion record. --contract 1 prints exactly what it did before.

changes.title: Notes and screenshots on phases and gates
changes.now: A phase can have a note and screenshots right under its heading, and a gate can have screenshots under its note. Runs show them in the phase header and the gate's panel.
changes.before: Notes and screenshots could only follow a step.
changes.where: The checklist editor and the run screen

changes.title: Suggest a change to a phase's note or a gate's
changes.now: Anyone viewing a run can suggest new wording for a phase's note or a gate's. It is decided and applied to the draft like a step's correction. Teammates on Flightdeck 1.22 or earlier see it as a described problem.
changes.before: Corrections could only be about a step.

changes.title: Gate notes now show in runs
changes.now: A gate's note shows above Pass the gate, for every version, including versions published before 2.0.
changes.before: Gate notes were published but no run screen showed them.

changes.title: The publish panel says when a version needs Flightdeck 2.0
changes.now: When a checklist uses something new in 2.0, the publish panel names it and says what that means: teammates on Flightdeck 1.22 or earlier see the version but can't run it. A checklist that uses nothing new publishes as before, and every teammate runs it.

changes.title: Run an exact version of another checklist
changes.now: A {run.process} step can say version: N, and a run made with Flightdeck 2.0 follows the version it started with for every linked run, even after a newer one is published. If that version can't be used, the step says why instead of starting another one.
changes.before: A linked run always started on the latest version.
changes.where: Checklists and the run screen

changes.title: Continue an older run with Flightdeck 2.0
changes.now: When a run made before 2.0 reaches a step whose linked checklist needs Flightdeck 2.0, it offers Start it as a Flightdeck 2.0 run. The old step is marked Continued in run <key>, which teammates on older copies read too.
changes.before: An older run could start a linked run older copies couldn't open.

changes.title: Plans that start on an exact version
changes.now: A plan for a version made with Flightdeck 2.0 starts on that version and nothing else. If it can't be used, the plan asks, and Start on vN instead switches it on purpose.
changes.before: A plan fell back to the latest version by itself.

changes.title: Register skills with flightdeck skill register
changes.now: flightdeck skill register writes the skill's registration for a version made with Flightdeck 2.0, and a {run.skill} step can say skillVersion: to expect one. Checking the step records which registration was current, with a warning if it isn't the expected one.
changes.before: Skills were registered by hand in skills/<name>.json.

changes.title: Evidence checks pins and the published payload
changes.now: Evidence for a run made with Flightdeck 2.0 checks that its version's pins and payload match what was published, and step fingerprints include the version each step runs.
changes.before: Pins weren't part of the evidence.

changes.title: See reports from tools on each step, and accept or decline them
changes.now: A tool or script that did a step's work can write a report with flightdeck report write. The step shows what the report says, what a person decided, and whether its inputs match the run. The recorder can accept a passing report, which checks the step with exactly its evidence, or decline it with a reason.
changes.before: A tool's work could only be recorded by a person typing it in.
changes.where: The selected step in a run, and Reports beside Follow-ups

changes.title: Receipts and Evidence show which reports were accepted
changes.now: The receipt names the report a step was accepted from, with its hash, and lists every report on the run. Evidence export packs the run's reports and the decisions on them.
changes.before: There were no reports.

headline: Back and Forward work inside Flightdeck

changes.title: Back and Forward work inside Flightdeck
changes.before: The browser's Back button left Flightdeck.
changes.now: Back and Forward move between screens, runs and the receipt. Back closes an open dialog first, and never loses what you typed.
changes.where: Everywhere; Alt+Left and Alt+Right work too

changes.title: The builder edits a checklist's details, step notes and Questions
changes.before: The builder sent you to the Markdown to list roles and run details, set the owner, change a step's note, or answer and remove a Questions section.
changes.now: Checklist details, at the top of the outline, sets the owner and backup owner and adds or removes roles and run details. Each step's form has its note. The Questions section opens in a panel where you edit it, then Remove section clears it for publishing. Undo works on all of them.
changes.where: Process › Edit › Builder

headline: Ready for teammates on Flightdeck 2.0

changes.title: Files made with Flightdeck 2.0 say so
changes.before: A version or run from a newer Flightdeck said only "Update Flightdeck to run it".
changes.now: Versions and runs made with Flightdeck 2.0 say "Needs Flightdeck 2.0". A test run from Flightdeck 2.0 says so too. This copy still shows them by name and never changes them.
changes.where: Process pages, Runs and the run itself

changes.title: See what a newer Flightdeck wrote, and who is on an older one
changes.now: Folder health lists each file a newer Flightdeck wrote, by kind, with the version it needs. It also names older copies of Flightdeck that answered connection checks or edited drafts here in the last 7 days, and says to move every computer to this version before anyone uses Flightdeck 2.0 features.
changes.where: Folder health

changes.title: Decisions from a newer Flightdeck aren't read as older ones
changes.before: A follow-up or correction decision saved by a newer Flightdeck was read as if this copy had written it.
changes.now: A decision from a newer Flightdeck is no longer read as if it were an older one. It's listed as needing a newer Flightdeck, and the follow-up or correction stays as it was.

changes.title: A "format:" line no longer passes for a requirement
changes.before: A checklist with a "format:" or "features:" line in its front matter published as an ordinary version.
changes.now: A checklist with a "format:" or "features:" line can't be published until the line is removed, and the editor says why. Nothing in a checklist needs one.

changes.title: Plans from a newer Flightdeck are named, never started on the wrong version
changes.now: A planned run saved by Flightdeck 2.0 for one exact version isn't shown as a plan here, so it can't start on the latest by mistake. Folder health lists it as needing Flightdeck 2.0.

headline: Let another app ask for a run

changes.title: Ask for a run from another app: flightdeck plan request
changes.now: A script or another app can ask for a run with flightdeck plan request and a key, such as the month. It shows under Runs as a planned run. A person starts it, changes it or declines it; nothing starts by itself. Asking again with the same key and the same request changes nothing, and the same key with other details is refused.
changes.where: The flightdeck command, then Runs

changes.title: See which tool asked for a planned run
changes.now: A planned run another app asked for says "requested by" the tool, by its own account. The name is what the file says, so Flightdeck reminds you it can't confirm who wrote it.
changes.where: Runs, Home and the start form

changes.title: Copies of a planned run and double starts are shown
changes.before: When OneDrive kept two copies of a planned run, it showed twice. A plan started on two computers at once showed as started once.
changes.now: Copies that say the same thing show once, marked as arrived twice. Copies that differ are both flagged and can't be started until someone deletes the wrong one. A plan started twice shows that its decisions disagree, so you can check Runs.

headline: Edit a checklist with your AI assistant at the same time

changes.title: See your AI assistant's changes as you edit
changes.now: When your AI assistant changes a draft you have open with nothing unsaved, its change appears in the editor within a few seconds, marked "Changed by your AI assistant", and is saved. One Undo takes it back. Otherwise it waits for you on the process page. From another computer, add OneDrive's time. With the draft open on two computers, use Decline there rather than Undo.
changes.where: Edit on a process page

changes.title: Add screenshots to a step in the builder
changes.before: To show a screenshot with a step, you copied the image into images/ yourself and typed its line in Markdown.
changes.now: Select a step and add screenshots in its form: choose files, drop them there, or paste one. Each needs a caption, which is also what screen readers say. Edit captions, move screenshots up or down, or remove one from the draft; the image file stays in the folder. Undo takes back any of it, and nothing is saved until you save the draft.
changes.where: Edit on a process page, then select a step

changes.title: Undo a newer draft that arrived
changes.before: When a newer draft arrived while you had nothing unsaved, the editor took it and your earlier changes couldn't be undone.
changes.now: A newer draft arrives as one change you can undo, and the changes before it can still be undone.

changes.title: Proposed changes wait for you
changes.now: When a draft is open in an editor, or changed since your AI assistant read it, its changes arrive as a proposal. Review it, then Apply or Decline it on the process page. Apply works only when the proposal starts from the draft as it is now; anything else waits for you to look at it.
changes.where: A process page

changes.title: See who's editing a draft
changes.now: A draft open in someone's editor shows who and on which computer, as far as this computer can see right now. You can still edit it, and each save is checked against the draft you opened.

changes.title: flightdeck draft read, save and propose
changes.now: AI assistants read and save drafts with the flightdeck command. When someone has the draft open, it sends a proposal instead of writing over their work.

changes.title: Saves check the exact text
changes.now: Saving a draft checks that the file is still exactly the text you started from, right before writing, not only a short fingerprint of it.

changes.title: Drafts up to 1 MB
changes.now: Drafts are saved up to 1 MB. A bigger one isn't saved: Flightdeck says how much to cut and keeps your text. From 0.9 MB the editor shows the size.

headline: Other apps can read checklists, runs, what's waiting and follow-ups as JSON

changes.title: Read checklists and runs as JSON
changes.now: Scripts and other apps can read the team folder as a teammate would: flightdeck processes, process, runs, run, next and followups, with --json. They show checklists, runs, what's waiting and on whom, and follow-ups. They only read and never change the folder. Anything they couldn't read is named file by file, with exit code 4. People-directory email fields are omitted.
changes.where: flightdeck run <team folder> <process>/<run id> --json, and docs/apps.md

changes.title: Copy a run's key
changes.now: Copy run key copies the key other apps use to read a run, like backup-check/k3m9p2q8.
changes.where: A run's More menu

changes.title: See each phase's steps in the flight plan
changes.before: Each phase showed only how many steps it had.
changes.now: Each phase lists its steps: the type, the text, must-dos, who does it, the skill that covers it, lanes side by side, and the gate last. Choose a step to open it in the checklist. Show all steps or Hide all steps opens or closes every phase. Phases start open when the checklist has 40 steps or fewer. Your choice is kept for each process in this browser.
changes.where: A process page, Flight plan

headline: Search everything with Ctrl+K, and big team folders open and refresh faster, show 50 runs at a time, and warn when refreshing is slow

changes.title: Search everything with Ctrl+K
changes.now: Press Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac), or / when single-key shortcuts are on. Find runs, steps, notes, corrections, follow-ups, step types, skills and pages, grouped by kind, with your words highlighted. Accents don't matter. Choose a result to go straight there; anything you were typing is kept. Results update as the folder changes, and a run that couldn't be read is found from its last copy and marked.
changes.where: Search in the top bar, on every page

changes.title: Export a run's evidence
changes.now: Make an evidence pack of one run, or of a process's runs between two days: a zip with the original files, a page to read, and SHA-256 hashes to check them by. It says what it left out and why, and anything that changed while it was made. Save it, and keep its SHA-256 somewhere separate. The people directory is left out; the records may still name people.
changes.where: A run's Receipt or its More menu, and Runs › Export evidence…

changes.title: flightdeck export
changes.now: flightdeck export makes the same evidence pack from the command line, for one run (--run) or for the runs started between two days (--process, --from, --through, in --tz). It never changes the team folder, prints the pack's SHA-256, and exits 0 for a complete pack, 4 for a partial one and 1 when it made none.
changes.where: flightdeck export <team folder> --run <process>/<run id>

changes.title: How runs go counts runs, one version at a time, and says what it left out
changes.before: Numbers mixed versions when phases shared a name, counted every answer instead of every run, and lost blocks whose answers were archived. Runs that couldn't be read were counted without a word.
changes.now: Each number belongs to one version, counts runs, and says how many runs it's out of and which it couldn't count, and why. Unreadable or future times and reopened gates are left out of times. Choose a number to see its runs. Known limit: a time that can't be read is dropped when any copy saves the run, as before, so it's left out only until then.
changes.where: A process › How runs go, and the flight plan

changes.title: Filter runs
changes.now: Narrow the Runs page by process, version, outcome and the dates runs started. Each filter shows as a chip you can remove.
changes.where: Runs › Filter runs

changes.title: Runs load 50 at a time
changes.before: The Runs page drew every run at once, which got slow with hundreds of runs.
changes.now: Running and Finished each show 50 runs and say how many there are. Show 50 more adds the next ones and moves you to the first one added.
changes.where: Runs

changes.title: Says when refreshing is slow on this computer
changes.now: When the last 3 refreshes each took more than 15 seconds, Folder health says how long refreshing takes here, with what to do about a big folder.
changes.where: Settings › Folder health

changes.title: Big team folders open faster, and show runs as they're read
changes.before: Opening a team folder checked every file's size before and after reading it, showed no runs until all of them were read, and read and shrank every picture on a page at once.
changes.now: Reading a file now gives its size too, so opening a big folder asks OneDrive about half as many things. Runs appear as they're read, and Home and Runs say "Still reading runs (640 of 2,000)" until it's done. A run not read yet is never shown as gone. Pictures are read when they scroll into view, a few at a time, after the run you're recording.
changes.where: Opening a team folder, Home, Runs, and any page with pictures

changes.title: Refreshing a big team folder asks for much less
changes.before: Every refresh checked every file in every run, about 10,000 checks for a folder of 2,000 runs, every 30 seconds.
changes.now: Running runs and runs that ended in the last week are checked on every refresh. Older runs are checked a share at a time, each one at least every 10 minutes, so a refresh asks OneDrive about 80% fewer things. A late note on an old run can take up to 10 minutes to show. Refresh in the top bar still reads everything at once.
changes.where: Every team folder, while Flightdeck is open

changes.title: An edit that keeps a file's size and time still shows up
changes.before: A finished run was read again only when one of its files changed size or time, so an edit that kept both never showed until you chose Refresh.
changes.now: Every finished run is read in full at least once an hour, and every running run you don't have open at least every 5 minutes, whatever its size and time say. Decisions on corrections and follow-ups are read again at least once an hour too.
changes.where: Every team folder, while Flightdeck is open

changes.title: Changing the clock or waking from sleep no longer delays refreshing
changes.before: If the computer's clock was set back, Flightdeck stopped refreshing until the clock caught up again.
changes.now: Setting the clock back doesn't delay refreshing, and after the computer sleeps, Flightdeck refreshes as soon as you come back and reads whatever went past its time first. While the tab is hidden nothing is read.
changes.where: Every team folder, while Flightdeck is open

headline: Make the editors' side panels wider or narrower

changes.title: Resize the Run preview
changes.before: The Run preview beside the step-type form had a fixed width.
changes.now: Drag the line between the form and the preview to make the preview wider or narrower. Or focus the line and use the Left and Right arrow keys (Shift moves further), Home and End. Enter or a double-click puts it back. The form always keeps room. Your width is kept in this browser only.
changes.where: Step types › a step type, the line left of Run preview

changes.title: Resize the parts and the inspector
changes.before: The builder's Parts list and the inspector had fixed widths.
changes.now: The Parts list and the inspector each have a line you can drag or move with the arrow keys, the same way as the step-type preview, and each keeps its own width. The Markdown view uses the inspector's width too. When the parts are folded to icons, only the inspector resizes.
changes.where: A process page › Edit, the lines beside Parts and the inspector

changes.title: The step-type form has its room again
changes.before: On a wide screen the step-type form was squeezed into a narrow column and the Run preview took most of the page.
changes.now: The form takes most of the page and the preview is a narrower column beside it, as intended.
changes.where: Step types › a step type

changes.title: Dialogs fit the window
changes.before: On a short window, the Keyboard shortcuts dialog ran off the bottom and hid its Close button.
changes.now: Dialogs stay inside the window and scroll when their content is longer.
changes.where: Keyboard shortcuts, and History

changes.title: Opens in a browser that blocks site storage
changes.before: In a browser set to block site data, Flightdeck stopped while setting up the examples and showed nothing.
changes.now: The examples open, and a short dialog explains once that they and your changes to them last only while the tab is open. After that, a Tab only badge at the top of the window stays in view on every screen, dialog and phone step panel. The run's save status and the editors' labels say Saved in this tab only. A team folder still keeps everything.
changes.where: Opening Flightdeck

headline: Apply a correction to the draft, then see which version has it

changes.title: Review and apply
changes.before: A correction could only be marked as applied. Someone had to make the change in the draft by hand, or with an AI assistant, and nothing checked that the draft had it.
changes.now: Review and apply shows what the run's version said, the draft now and the result side by side, then makes the change in the draft and saves it. Only that step changes. If the step changed since the run, you edit or confirm the result first. If the draft already has it, Link this correction records that. A screenshot or a described problem opens the editor at that step instead.
changes.where: A process page › Corrections › Review and apply

changes.title: Choose between two proposals, or combine them
changes.now: When people suggested different wording for one step, use one of them, or combine them into your own wording. Combining marks each of them as applied.
changes.where: Review and apply, on a step with two proposed changes

changes.title: Undo an applied correction
changes.now: Applying is one change in the draft editor's history, named for the step, so Undo takes it back. The draft then has unsaved changes until you save it.
changes.where: The Undo button in the message, or the draft editor's Undo and History

changes.title: Changed since applied
changes.now: A correction applied in Flightdeck remembers what the step said. If the step changes again in the draft, the correction says Changed since applied.
changes.where: A process page › Corrections › All

changes.title: Steps with open corrections are marked while you edit
changes.before: Only the preview marked steps with open corrections.
changes.now: The builder's rows say how many open corrections a step has. The Markdown view lists them above the text, with Go to line for each.
changes.where: A process page › Edit

changes.title: Published in vN
changes.before: An applied correction said Applied to draft forever. Nothing said which version had it.
changes.now: Publishing records which applied corrections the new version includes. A correction then says Published in v5, but only when v5 both lists it and really says it; a later version with other edits never counts. The publish panel says how many corrections the version includes and names any that changed since they were applied.
changes.where: A process page › Draft › Publish, and Corrections › All

changes.title: Changed in vN, and why
changes.now: In runs of the version that first has a correction, its step says Changed in v5. Why is this here? shows what it said before and after, the reason, the runs that suggested it and who applied it.
changes.where: A run › the step's row and the selected step

changes.title: Hear back about your corrections
changes.now: When a correction you suggested is published, Home says so once per version, with View change. When someone declines one, Home says who and why. Dismiss hides it in this browser.
changes.where: Home › Your corrections

changes.title: Say which version has an older correction
changes.now: For a correction applied before 1.16, Flightdeck says it can't confirm which version has it. It's in v5 records that, and Flightdeck still checks that v5 makes the change.
changes.where: A process page › Corrections › All

changes.title: The correction brief quotes what the step said and what was proposed
changes.now: The brief for your AI assistant quotes From and Proposed as data, lists attached files' paths, and leaves out corrections already published.
changes.where: A process page › Corrections › Copy correction brief

changes.title: Say what became of a follow-up
changes.before: Follow-ups showed on Home for 30 days and then disappeared, done or not.
changes.now: Mark a follow-up Done (with a link or note), Moved to a ticket, Moved to another run or plan, or Won't do (with a reason), and Reopen it if that changes. Anyone on the team can. Two people deciding at once shows as Needs review.
changes.where: A run › Follow-ups, Home › Your follow-ups, and Runs › Follow-ups

changes.title: Your open follow-ups stay until they're dealt with
changes.before: Home listed every follow-up from runs that ended in the last 30 days.
changes.now: Home lists the open follow-ups you own, however old. Once one is done, moved or won't be done, it drops off.
changes.where: Home › Your follow-ups

changes.title: Every follow-up in one list
changes.now: See open follow-ups across all runs, oldest first, with who owns each, how long it's been open and its run. Switch to Yours or All.
changes.where: Runs › Follow-ups

changes.title: Follow-ups show where they stand
changes.now: The receipt and the finish page show each follow-up's status, and the text you copy for Jira says what became of it.
changes.where: A run › Receipt

changes.title: Follow-ups open for more than 30 days
changes.now: Folder health lists follow-ups that have been open for more than 30 days as worth a look, with Review follow-ups.
changes.where: Settings › Folder health

changes.title: The example release watches new pods for 20 minutes everywhere
changes.before: An example correction proposed watching new pods for 20 minutes while the step's expected result and timing said 10.
changes.now: The example step's expected result and timing say 20 minutes, and the correction its runs suggest puts the same 20 minutes in its wording.
changes.where: The examples › Production release

changes.title: Saved history
changes.before: History listed only the changes made in this window, and they were gone once it closed.
changes.now: History has a This session | Saved history switch. Saved history lists every save of the draft kept in the team folder, from every computer, newest first: who saved it, how (saved, restored from a version, applied a correction), what changed, and where each version was published. A change made outside Flightdeck, by hand or by an AI assistant, is marked where it happened.
changes.where: The draft editor › History › Saved history

changes.title: Reverse a saved change
changes.now: Reverse this change takes one saved change back out of the draft, if the lines it added are still there exactly. The draft then has unsaved changes, and Undo takes the reversal back. If the text changed since, Compare shows the change so you can edit it yourself.
changes.where: The draft editor › History › Saved history

changes.title: Saved history of a step type
changes.now: A step type's History has Saved history too, with each save's changes field by field. A field's History shows only its own.
changes.where: Step types › a type › History

headline: Team confidence: Folder health, a connection check between computers, and safer updates and backups

changes.title: Folder health
changes.now: Flightdeck checks every file in the team folder on request and lists what needs a person: conflict copies, OneDrive's second copies, files that can't be read, versions that never finished arriving, runs left for a week, clocks that are off, a folder getting too big. Each has one button for what to do. Home says when something needs action.
changes.where: Settings › Folder health, or a run's More menu

changes.title: Check the connection between two computers
changes.now: Send a check from one computer and watch the other answer, with each leg timed and whether both have the same revision of the latest run. While the page is open it answers checks by itself; elsewhere a banner offers Answer. If the two clocks differ, it says by how much at least.
changes.where: Settings › Connection check

changes.title: What to do, inside Flightdeck
changes.now: The guide for when something goes wrong (conflict copies, lost folder access, OneDrive not syncing, restoring a backup, someone leaving) is in the app. Folder health, a run's conflict copies and the top bar's "can't read it" link straight to the right section.
changes.where: Settings › When something goes wrong

changes.title: install sets up the whole folder, and keeps your changes
changes.before: flightdeck install copied only flightdeck.html. The skills were a separate command, and skills --force replaced files your team had changed without keeping a copy.
changes.now: flightdeck install also adds or updates AGENTS.md and the skills for your AI assistant. Files still at an earlier default are updated; files your team changed are kept. When this version changed them too, the new default goes to .flightdeck/updates/1.15.0/ with a README.md to hand to your AI assistant. Add --app-only to install only the app.
changes.where: flightdeck install <team folder>

changes.title: See what an update would do first
changes.now: Add --check to install or skills to see what would change, without changing anything. It exits with 0 when there's nothing to do, 2 when updates are ready, and 3 when files need merging, so a script can tell.
changes.where: flightdeck install <team folder> --check

changes.title: Back up a team folder
changes.now: flightdeck backup copies the whole team folder to a dated folder in Flightdeck backups in your home folder, or wherever you name with --to. It never copies links and never puts a backup inside the folder it backs up.
changes.where: flightdeck backup <team folder>

changes.title: Install keeps a copy of every file it replaces
changes.now: Before install or skills replaces any file, even with --force, it saves the old one under .flightdeck/updates/<version>/replaced/ and checks the copy, so nothing your team had is lost.
changes.where: flightdeck install or skills

changes.title: AGENTS.md has a place for your team's own notes
changes.now: Flightdeck's instructions for AI assistants sit between two markers in AGENTS.md. Team notes, below them, are yours: updates never change them.
changes.where: AGENTS.md in the team folder

changes.title: A new team folder's starter checklist names you as owner
changes.before: Start a new team folder made the starter Check in code checklist with an example person as its owner.
changes.now: The starter checklist names whoever created the folder as its owner, and the folder records which Flightdeck set it up.
changes.where: Settings: Start a new team folder

changes.title: A file that can't be read is listed, not lost from view
changes.before: A run whose file couldn't be read disappeared from every list, a draft that couldn't be read looked deleted, and one file that couldn't be read stopped the whole folder from loading.
changes.now: The run or draft stays as last read and says its file couldn't be read; nothing is changed or saved over it until it reads again. The Runs page, the run itself and Folder health name the file, and the rest of the folder loads as usual.

changes.title: Two drafts for one process are both shown
changes.before: When two drafts said the same process (often a OneDrive copy like release-LAPTOP.md), only one was shown.
changes.now: The process page lists both and says which one it shows, so you settle it before publishing. Folder health lists them too.

changes.title: Step types and skills past the limit are reported
changes.before: Past 100 step-type files or 500 skill registrations, the rest were quietly left out.
changes.now: The first ones by name are read, and the Step types and Skills pages and Folder health say how many weren't.

changes.title: A deleted run is never written back by itself
changes.before: If someone deleted or moved a run's file while it was open in another window, that window's next change quietly wrote the run back.
changes.now: The run says its file is gone from the team folder, the Runs page marks it, and nothing is saved. Restore it here writes it back only when you choose it, and the run's log says so.
changes.where: The run, and Settings › Folder health

changes.title: A run file that reads again stops saying it can't be read
changes.before: If a save found the run's file unreadable for a moment, the run kept saying its file couldn't be read, and refused new changes, even after the file read fine again, until Try again saved the waiting change.
changes.now: As soon as the file reads again, the run says so and takes changes again. Your waiting change stays on screen with Try again until it's saved.

changes.title: Start your team, join, or look around
changes.now: The first screen offers Start your team, Join your team's folder and Look around the examples. Starting walks you through five steps: a shared folder Flightdeck checks it can save in, your people and a backup owner, a first checklist, a first run on your own, and a second computer.
changes.where: The first screen; Settings, Start a new team

changes.title: Getting started on Home until your team is set up
changes.now: The folder owner sees Getting started, N of 5, with Continue on the next step. Each step ticks itself from what's in the team folder, and a stamp says when your team is set up.
changes.where: Home

changes.title: Join a team folder and choose who you are
changes.now: Open the team's folder and pick your name from its people. Not on the list? Copy a request to the folder owner. Joining never changes the people list.
changes.where: The first screen, Join your team's folder

changes.title: A folder owner and backup owner keep the people list
changes.now: The folder owner and backup owner add people, mark them inactive or active, and choose the backup in Settings. IDs are made from names once and never change, and nobody is ever deleted. A change is refused if people.json changed since you opened the page. Roles prevent ordinary mistakes; they aren't security.
changes.before: You edited people.json by hand.
changes.where: Settings, People

changes.title: A backup owner can sign off while the owner is away
changes.now: A checklist can name a backup: owner. While its owner is inactive or gone from the people list, the backup owner signs off versions as ready for a skill. Folder health says when a checklist or the folder needs a new owner.

headline: Five new step types: Jira sprints, deploys, health checks, GitHub pull requests and measurements

changes.title: Jira sprint steps
changes.now: A {jira.sprint} step starts or closes a sprint, moves its unfinished issues, or sets its goal, on a named board. Checking it can note the sprint link, plus the new sprint's name and dates when starting, or how many issues carried over when closing.
changes.where: The parts box and the Type list in the draft editor, under Tools.

changes.title: Deploy and health check steps
changes.now: A {deploy} step names the environment, what to deploy, its version, the deploy tool and what to roll back to; checking it can note the version that went out, a link and when it finished. A {verify.health} step names a dashboard, a metric, when it counts as healthy and how long to watch; checking it can note Pass or Fail, the value you saw and a screenshot or link.
changes.where: The parts box and the Type list in the draft editor, under Tools.

changes.title: GitHub pull request steps
changes.now: A {github.pr} step opens, reviews, approves or merges a pull request in a named repository. Checking it can note the pull request link, whether its checks pass, and the merge commit for a merge.
changes.where: The parts box and the Type list in the draft editor, under Tools.

changes.title: Measure steps
changes.now: A {measure} step records a number with its unit, like velocity or points carried over, so runs keep a history of it. When later steps need the number as a run detail, use a step with sets: instead, like the capacity step in the sprint start example.
changes.where: The parts box and the Type list in the draft editor, under General.

changes.title: The examples use the new types
changes.now: The sprint start example closes the last sprint, records velocity, carry-over and capacity, then starts the new sprint and sets its goal. The release example records the deploy and watches the error dashboard. A new example merges a GitHub pull request. Versions that use the new types still open and run in earlier copies of Flightdeck.
changes.where: The example folder.

headline: Fill in keeps the evidence you typed, and Done differently tells the truth about a refused save

changes.title: Fill in keeps evidence typed before it opened
changes.before: If you typed evidence on a step, then opened Fill in and saved it, Fill in started with empty evidence boxes and saving threw away what you had typed. Done then checked the step without it.
changes.now: Fill in starts with the evidence you already typed on the step, and saving it keeps that evidence with the step. Done records it.
changes.where: A run: the selected step, Record the result, Fill in.

changes.title: Done differently no longer says it saved when it didn't
changes.before: If the run was saved from another window or computer while Done differently was saving its correction, the step stayed unanswered in the team folder but Flightdeck said "Done differently… Saved on this computer."
changes.now: Flightdeck says the run changed elsewhere and shows "Correction saved; the step wasn't marked done." with Mark it now, which stays on the run until you act. If the save failed and is waiting for Try again, it says that instead.
changes.where: A run: Done differently.

headline: Runs get a workspace of their own, corrections replace Suggest a fix, and notes take files

changes.title: A run fills the window
changes.before: A run was a long page: a big header, details, roles and a recording banner pushed the steps below the fold, and the step panel scrolled with everything else.
changes.now: A run is a page of its own: a slim header with 7/14 answered, a strip saying who's recording with Pause, Hand off, Pick up or Take over beside it, then three panes that each scroll on their own: Phases, the checklist and the selected step. The strip also says what this window saved and when it checked the folder; a failed save or a conflict shows there with Try again or Compare copies.
changes.where: Runs: open any run.

changes.title: Next up, and one place to answer a step
changes.now: Next up, pinned atop the checklist, points at where the run stands (the next step, a blocked step, a gate to review), never at what you're looking at. The selected step shows how to do it, values to copy, evidence to record, Done, Blocked, N/A and notes. Done reads what you typed in its evidence boxes. Check the step Next up points at and the next one is selected, so Space keeps going.
changes.where: A run: the checklist and the selected step.

changes.title: Suggest a fix became Corrections
changes.before: Suggest a fix asked you to pick one of several kinds of problem, then describe it in your own words. The process page marked a suggestion fixed whenever any newer version was published.
changes.now: Correct this step starts on the wording, with a Before/After redline as you type; Change something else covers a missing step, the order, who does it, a screenshot or removing it. It never answers the step. Runs and receipts list their Corrections; on the process page the same one from several runs shows once, and anyone marks it applied or declines it with a reason.
changes.where: A run: Correct this step on the selected step (or press C). A process page: Corrections.

changes.title: Done differently
changes.now: Beside Done, the recorder can mark a step Done differently: say what happened, then choose Just this run or Fix the checklist too, which adds a correction. It follows every rule of Done, so required evidence still has to be there.
changes.where: A run: the selected step.

changes.title: What you type stays with its step
changes.now: Evidence typed into a step, an open Fill in and an unsent note stay with that step while you move around the run, and come back when you return; the row says Draft. Drafts belong to their team folder. Checking a step (row, Done, Space or Done differently) uses what was typed on that step only. While its Fill in is open or unsaved, Done waits and says "Save or cancel Fill in first."
changes.where: A run.

changes.title: Attachments with runs of dots in their names
changes.now: A file named like deploy..output.log is saved as deploy.output.log and stays listed with its note after a reload.
changes.where: A run: attachments on notes and corrections.

changes.title: Attach files to notes and corrections
changes.before: A note or a suggested fix could carry one PNG, JPEG or WebP screenshot.
changes.now: Drop files on the note box, paste them, or choose Attach: images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF), PDF, text and logs (.txt, .log, .md, .csv, .json, .yaml) and .zip, up to 10 MB each and several per note. Images show as pictures; text opens as plain text; other files save a copy. A file that isn't allowed is refused next to the box with the reason.
changes.where: A run: the selected step's notes, or Correct this step.

changes.title: Keyboard, phones and screen share
changes.now: J and K open a folded phase they move into, X works like Space, and a held key checks one step. On a phone a step opens as a full-screen sheet with Close, Previous and Next. Screen share shows who's recording, a pause, and why a step is blocked; Back to the run returns to the same step and scroll.
changes.where: A run. Press ? for the keys.

changes.title: Plain words for your AI assistant
changes.before: Skill briefs and the Skills page used a technical term for the assistant that builds skills.
changes.now: Flightdeck now says "your AI assistant" everywhere: copy the brief for your AI assistant, and it builds or updates the skill.
changes.where: Skills, and a process page: Skills.

headline: Build a checklist from parts, with Undo, Redo and History in every editor and a clearer step-type editor

changes.title: The draft editor is a page of its own
changes.now: Editing a draft fills the window: a header with Done, save state, Builder or Markdown, Undo, Redo and History, Checks and Save, then side-by-side panes that each scroll on their own. The inspector has Selected, Checks and Preview tabs, and Preview marks the selected step. Parts fold to a rail of icons. A refresh comes back to the editor, and the browser asks before leaving unsaved edits.
changes.where: A process page: Edit.

changes.title: A parts box beside the builder
changes.now: Add phases, parallel lanes, gates and any type of step from a searchable parts box. Drag a part onto the checklist: only places it can go light up and the nearest says where it lands. Or choose a part, pick a place with the arrow keys, and press Enter. The new item is selected with its name ready to type over, and Undo takes it back.
changes.where: A process page: Edit, then the Builder. On a phone, Add part.

changes.title: Edit lanes, gates and phases in the builder
changes.now: Parallel lanes show side by side. Select a lane to rename it, change who works it, or delete it, keeping its steps or deleting them with it. A phase's form can delete the phase or remove its gate. A step's kind is one choice: Step, Must do or Automation planned. A part you just added takes its ID from the name you give it, until you save the draft.
changes.where: A process page: Edit, then select a lane or phase in the Builder.

changes.title: Undo, Redo and History in the checklist editor
changes.before: Only the builder had Undo. Typing in Markdown or saving the draft cleared it.
changes.now: Undo, Redo and History sit beside the Builder | Markdown switch, in both views, with one history for both. Undo names what it takes back, like Undo move, and says what it undid. Ctrl+Z or Cmd+Z undoes, Ctrl+Shift+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y redoes, even while typing. Undo still works after a save; saving again is checked like any save.
changes.where: A process page: Edit. A selected step or phase also has History of this step or phase.

changes.title: Undo, Redo and History in the step-type form
changes.now: The step-type form has the same Undo, Redo and History and the same keys. Removing a field or evidence and undoing puts it back where it was, with everything it had. Each row has its own History.
changes.where: Step types: New step type, or Edit on a team type.

changes.title: A clearer step-type editor
changes.before: One long form: the ID first, hints between labels and boxes, every field crammed on one line, and a Save button that was disabled without saying why.
changes.now: A full page with Save, Undo and History at the top and a live preview of the type in a checklist and in a run. The ID comes from the label. Tags are chips, the icon is a grid, and each field is a card you open, reorder or remove. Save says what's missing and keeps you in the editor, and Done asks before you lose changes.
changes.where: Step types: New step type, or Edit on a team type.

changes.title: Undo never puts older text over newer work
changes.now: When the draft changes in the folder, or you take their version, restore a version or discard your changes, History marks the spot and Undo stops there. Changes before it stay listed but can't be undone, so Undo never brings older text back over someone else's work.

changes.title: Checklist, Flight plan or Markdown in one switch
changes.before: Markdown was a separate small button beside the Checklist | Flight plan switch, and it didn't show when it was on.
changes.now: The checklist panel has one switch: Checklist, Flight plan or Markdown. Markdown shows the version's source, read-only, with Copy. The choice stays while you move around.
changes.where: A process page, the checklist panel.

headline: Checklist versions this copy can't read are never run

changes.title: Versions this copy doesn't understand can't be started
changes.before: A checklist version written by a newer Flightdeck, or edited by hand or by an AI assistant with lines or step types this copy doesn't know, was listed like any other version. You could start or plan a run on it, and steps that shouldn't have applied showed as ordinary work.
changes.now: Such a version isn't offered to start, plan or pick. The process page and the version picker say why: update Flightdeck to run it. A plan made for it starts on the latest version you can run, and says so. A run started on it, or saved by a newer copy with details or a file format this copy doesn't know, opens read-only with the reason, and this copy never saves over it or plans another like it.
changes.where: A process page, the version picker, Start a run, and the run page.

headline: Planned runs, a flight plan view, a checklist builder, and organized step types

changes.title: Suggest a fix to the checklist
changes.now: Anyone in a run can suggest a fix to the checklist from a step, a phase or a screenshot: a missing step, wrong instructions, a bad screenshot (attach the right one), wrong order, wrong role, or something else. On the process page, anyone can accept or decline each one with a reason. Accepted ones show as fixed once a newer version is published. Copy fix brief hands them to your AI assistant.
changes.where: A run: Suggest a fix on a step or phase. A process page: Suggested fixes.

changes.title: See a process as a flight plan
changes.now: On a process page, switch the checklist to Flight plan to see its shape at a glance: phases from start to landing, gates as checkpoints, tracks side by side and linked processes. With runs of that version, it shows each phase's usual time and the step that most often goes off-script. It marks steps covered by skills built from that version. Choose a phase to go to it.
changes.where: A process page, the Checklist | Flight plan switch.

changes.title: Edit a checklist with the builder
changes.now: Edit a draft as an outline: phases as cards, steps as rows, gates as striped bars. Drag a step, or select it and press Alt+Up or Alt+Down, to move it. Change a step's text, type, roles, run details and fields in the side form, and add steps, phases and gates. It writes the same Markdown, changing only the lines you touched and never a step ID. Markdown is one click away.

changes.title: Plan a run ahead of time
changes.now: Plan a run in the app: a name, the details you know, who does what and an optional time. Planned runs are listed by time under Runs and show on Home from a day before. Nothing starts until someone starts it.

changes.where: Starting a planned run.

changes.title: Step types in groups, with tags

Pick an older version to look back or restore it. How runs go has typical times and who has held each role.

changes.title: One place for the team folder and setup

headline: A README worth reading

changes.title: A full guide on the package page
changes.now: The README now walks through the loop from map to skill, a sixty-second tour of the examples, every feature, the map syntax with an example that publishes as written, process-to-skill traceability end to end, the command line, the team folder, the skills for your AI assistant, how Flightdeck stays safe, upgrading from Preflight, and an FAQ.

headline: Process-to-skill traceability, values that flow through a run, and a hierarchy for everything

changes.title: Preflight is now Flightdeck
changes.before: The app was called Preflight, in preflight.html, with AI assistant skills named preflight-*.
changes.now: It's Flightdeck: flightdeck.html, with AI assistant skills named flightdeck-*. Team folders, runs and versions carry over. A browser keeps examples and your name per file, so flightdeck.html starts those fresh; flightdeck install also updates an existing preflight.html, so people who open it keep everything.
changes.where: Everywhere.

changes.title: Install with npm
changes.now: npm install -g @troylar/flightdeck, then flightdeck open to try it, flightdeck install <team folder> to put the app there, and flightdeck skills <team folder> to add the skills for your AI assistant. No dependencies, nothing runs on install, no network.
changes.where: A terminal.

changes.title: See which skills implement each process
changes.now: Each process page lists the skills built from it: where each lives (any repo or folder), its own version, the process version it follows, and the steps it covers or the whole process. The map marks covered steps.
changes.where: Skills, on a process page; Home → Skills.

changes.title: Know when a process change affects a skill

changes.where: Copy update brief, on a skill.

changes.title: Prove a version, then turn it into a skill
changes.now: Each version shows its run evidence: completed runs, clean ones, and what people did differently. The flightdeck-skill-brief skill does the same from the folder, with your AI assistant.

changes.title: Organize processes and skills in a hierarchy, with tags
changes.now: Maps and skills say group: (like Engineering / Releases) and tags:. Home shows processes and skills as foldable trees, filtered by tag.
changes.where: Home → Processes and Skills.

The start form leaves it out and says which step fills it in. Correcting it later sends the steps that used the old value back for a re-check.

headline: Pause, parallel tracks, times, child runs, Jira fields and run history

changes.title: Pause and resume a run
changes.now: The recorder can pause a run and say what it's waiting for. While it's paused, steps and gates can't change and timers stop; Resume picks up where it left off, and paused time never counts in durations.
changes.where: Pause, in the recorder bar of a run.

changes.title: Work in parallel tracks
changes.now: A phase can split into tracks, each with its own role, shown side by side. Every track finishes before the phase's gate.

changes.where: Day timeline, under the run's headline.

changes.title: Run another process from a step
changes.now: A {run.process} step starts a linked run of another process, passing on the details it names. The parent step is checked when that run completes, or blocked if it stops, and the child links back to its parent.

changes.title: Check transitions against your real Jira workflow

changes.where: A Jira transition step; the process page shows the workflows.

changes.title: Add the team's own step types

changes.where: Team setup, on any process page.

changes.title: See how runs go and who has done each role

changes.where: How runs go, on a process page.

changes.title: Phase headers stay in view
changes.now: While you scroll through a phase, its header stays pinned under the top bar with the phase's progress, so you always know where you are.
changes.where: Any run.

changes.title: Redraw only what changed
changes.before: Every change redrew the whole screen.
changes.now: Only the parts of the screen that changed are redrawn, so focus, the caret and anything you're typing stay exactly where they were.

changes.title: Examples that show everything
changes.now: The examples now come with a month of team history: earlier releases (one stopped early) behind the analytics and role grid, a release whose check-in ran as a linked child run with its Jira fields filled in, an incident in progress split into tracks, and a sprint start that's paused, with its meeting time coming up.
changes.where: Home → Try the examples (Reset examples to see them in a browser that already has the old ones).

changes.title: Fewer leftover save receipts and copies

headline: See what's new, and know when a newer copy is waiting

changes.title: Read what changed in each version
changes.now: What's new in the top bar shows the version you're on and the full release history: search it, filter by new, improved or fixed and by area, and see before and after for each change. A dot appears when there's a release you haven't seen, and a short notice appears once after an update.
changes.where: What's new, in the top bar.

changes.title: Know when a newer Flightdeck is in the team folder

changes.where: The top bar, after opening or refreshing the team folder.

headline: Every save survives, on one computer or many

changes.title: Keep both versions when two windows save at once
changes.before: Two windows or computers saving the same run at the same moment could replace each other's change without a warning.
changes.now: Windows on one computer save a run one at a time. Across browsers and computers, each save first leaves its own receipt; a save that another one replaced shows up in the run as a conflict copy to compare and keep.
changes.where: The panel at the top of a run, when it has other versions.

changes.title: Give each window its own files
changes.now: Notes, history, plan decisions and screenshots are written by each window to its own files, so a duplicated tab or a second window can never overwrite them.

changes.title: Keep the newest change through slow refreshes and failed saves
changes.now: A refresh never brings back an older version of a run over a change you just made, a save still in progress, or one that failed. Try again always saves your newest change.

changes.title: Keep what you're still typing
changes.now: Finishing one note clears only that note. Text typed while it saved, other steps' drafts and their screenshots stay. Notes over 2,000 characters are refused with a message instead of being cut short.

headline: AI assistant skills for writing and improving maps

changes.title: Write, review and improve maps with your AI assistant
changes.now: Every team folder carries six skills for your AI assistant: write a new map, edit one, review one, learn from recent runs, plan a run and summarize the folder. A checker in the skills judges published versions and plan decisions exactly as Flightdeck does.
changes.where: Open the team folder with your AI assistant and ask for a skill by name, such as flightdeck-status.

changes.title: Start a new team folder with everything in it
changes.now: Start a new team folder adds you to people.json, a starter map, the guide for AI assistants and the Flightdeck skills. It refuses a folder that isn't empty.

headline: Finish runs well, recover safely, and work faster

changes.now: End run opens a short finish: add follow-ups with an owner and Jira ticket, review suggested map changes from "did it differently" answers and map-change notes, then choose the outcome. The receipt includes all of it, and follow-ups from the last 30 days show on Home.
changes.where: End run in any run you're recording.

changes.title: Compare and keep conflict copies in the app
changes.before: Conflict copies had to be compared by hand in the folder.
changes.now: A run with other versions shows a panel to compare each one, keep it (the current version is saved beside it first) or delete it. Nothing is merged without you choosing.

changes.title: Choose how to begin
changes.now: Home offers three paths: try the examples, open your team folder (with the OneDrive tip to keep it on this device), or start a new team folder.

changes.title: Run a checklist on your own
changes.now: Starting a run asks On my own or With others. Solo runs hide roles and screen sharing, and confirming a phase is one click.

changes.title: Refresh only what's open
changes.now: While a run is open, Flightdeck rereads just that run every few seconds. Published versions and finished runs are remembered, so large team folders stay quick.

changes.title: Easier with a keyboard and screen reader
changes.now: Single-key shortcuts can be turned off, dialogs return focus when closed, errors appear next to their field, form fields have stronger borders, and messages are announced.
changes.where: Press ? for keyboard help and the shortcut switch.

headline: Fill in values as they become known

changes.title: Fill in or correct a step's values mid-run
changes.now: Some values aren't known until the middle of a release. The recorder can fill in a step's details and evidence before or after checking it; each change is logged with its old value, and the map's own value stays visible.
changes.where: Fill in, on any step.

changes.title: Describe a step with only what's known
changes.before: A step type's usual fields were required before a map could publish.
changes.now: A step can name only what's known; a missing usual field is a tip, not an error. Evidence is required only where the map says require: or evidence:.

headline: Clearer headings and runs for one

changes.title: The same headings on every computer
changes.now: Headings use a built-in typeface, so Windows and Mac show the same thing, and code-style text is used only for commands, values and times.

changes.title: Runs for one person
changes.now: A run with nobody but you assigned drops the team wording, and a map can say runs: solo to skip assigning roles.

headline: Step types that fit the work

changes.title: Jenkins, pull request and Jira steps
changes.now: New step types for a Jenkins job, a Bitbucket pull request and a Jira issue, each with the fields that matter to it.

changes.title: Record evidence when you check a step
changes.now: Steps can record a build number, a pull request link, a decision or a review verdict. It shows on the step and on the receipt.

headline: Flightdeck

changes.title: Versioned process maps
changes.now: Write a process as a checklist map with phases and gates, publish it as a numbered version, and see every version with its change note and differences.

changes.title: Run a checklist together
changes.now: One person records while others follow along and add notes and screenshots. Gates approve exactly what they say, and changing a detail like the commit sends tied steps back for a re-check.

changes.title: Timers, deadlines and a receipt
changes.now: Start a step to time it, copy a deadline from the real tool to see a countdown, and copy a receipt into Jira when you're done.
